page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It is configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware features a dedicated Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.8 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. This processor consists of 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, AES cryptography, and BMI2. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the n2-standard-8 delivers average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic operations fall within the middle tier of tested servers. For instance, the server achieves average marks in software compilation, text processing, and database operations. However, certain workloads exhibit weaker relative performance. Single-core CPU benchmarks, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and multi-core Geekbench scores rank in the bottom 25 percent. Graphics-adjacent tasks like ray tracing and image processing, as well as prompt processing for small language models, also show weaker performance characteristics, highlighting a tradeoff when executing highly parallelized or specialized vector math without dedicated accelerators.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU execution, the n2-standard-8 offers stable qualitative cost efficiency for mainstream enterprise workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications such as static web serving, Redis key-value stores, standard database operations, and moderate software compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 4 physical cores and hyper-threading, it features a 33 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instructions. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows average performance for memory bandwidth, database operations, and static web serving, though it exhibits weaker results in single-core execution and multi-core ray tracing. This server is suited for balanced workloads such as web serving, Redis caching, and standard database operations.
